title: The minimum overlap constant of the square
statement: For a measurable f: [0,2]^2 -> [0,1] with integral 2 (half the area of the square), let g = 1 - f on the square and g = 0 outside, and let M(f) = sup over x in R^2 of the integral of f(t) g(t - x) dt, the largest overlap between the 'first half' f and a translate of the 'second half' g. Determine mu_sq = inf over f of M(f). This is the square version of Erdos's minimum overlap problem (split {1, ..., 2n} into two halves A and B of equal size and minimise the largest number of solutions of a - b = k); its one-dimensional constant mu = 0.380... is constant 1b of the optimization-constants repository. Known bounds: 1/4 <= mu_sq <= 150615/262144 = 0.574550...; find a step function with a smaller overlap.
submission: Text file: a 16 x 16 array of integers between 0 and 64 summing to 64 * 16^2 / 2 = 8192 (16 lines of 16 numbers): the step function f = entry/64 on the cells of side 1/8 of [0,2]^2. Other grids and denominators can be checked with the checker's M and DEN arguments.
score: the overlap M(f) of the step function, an exact rational number (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: a 16 x 16 step function with values in multiples of 1/64, found by projected gradient descent on a smoothed maximum from an 8 x 8 start (tools/overlap2d.py)

context: Erdos's minimum overlap problem asks how evenly {1, ..., 2n} can be split so that no difference is realised too often between the halves; it reduces to a continuous constant mu, with White's lower bound 0.379005 (arXiv:2201.05704) and upper bounds by Haugland (0.380927, arXiv:1609.08000) and later computer searches (repository constant 1b: 0.379005 <= mu <= 0.38085856). In the square the same question measures how well a region of half the area can avoid its complement under every translation. Two elementary bounds frame it: averaging over translations gives mu_sq >= (int f)(int g) / 16 = 1/4, and cylinders f(t_1, t_2) = F(t_1) give mu_sq <= 2 mu < 0.7618; our 16 x 16 step function already gives 0.5746, so genuinely two-dimensional sets do much better than cylinders.
references: P. Erdos, Some remarks on number theory, Riveon Lematematika 9 (1955) 45-48 (the minimum overlap problem)
J. K. Haugland, The minimum overlap problem revisited, arXiv:1609.08000
E. P. White, Erdos' minimum overlap problem, arXiv:2201.05704 (the lower bound 0.379005)
Optimization constants in mathematics, constant 1b (github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems), read 9 November 2026

novelty.verdict: new. No paper or table on a two-dimensional (or square) version of Erdos's minimum overlap problem was found; the one-dimensional constant (repository constant 1b) is the closest.
closest: The one-dimensional minimum overlap constant mu (Erdos; Haugland; repository constant 1b). The square constant mu_sq is a different quantity, between 1/4 and 2 mu.
novelty.benchmark: the benchmark has the one-dimensional constants 1a, 1c and 1d, not 1b, and nothing two-dimensional of this kind

first_values.note: For comparison: cylinder functions built from the best known one-dimensional functions give 2 mu, about 0.7617.

baseline.text: 150615/262144 = 0.574550... (16 x 16 step function with values in multiples of 1/64, `refs/overlap-square.txt`), held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026. Lower bound 1/4 from averaging the overlap over all translations (the translations x with nonzero overlap fill [-2,2]^2, of area 16, and the overlaps integrate to (int f)(int g) = 4).

bound.source: averaging over translations: integral over x of the overlap is 4, supported on [-2,2]^2 of area 16
